newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Health ministers to discuss tobacco curbs.
newsitem.headline: Health ministers to discuss tobacco curbs.

text.p: Health ministers will on Thursday discuss a European Commission report on ways to reduce tobacco consumption, but despite the new British government's anti-smoking stance no action is expected, EU diplomats said.
In December, EU Health Commissioner Padraig Flynn presented a report outlining options EU governments could take to curb smoking and its damaging health effects.

These included strengthening cigarette label warnings, reducing the tar and nicotine content of cigarettes, controlling additives and agreeing a code of practice on children's right to a smoke-free environment.
Governments were also urged to consider increasing taxes on cigarettes and making it more difficult for young people to buy cigarettes.

The new British Labour Government last month last month announced a national ban on cigarette advertising and plans to follow this up later in 1997 with a white paper containing a broader package of measures, diplomats said.

Britain's Public Health Minister, Tessa Jowell, is expected during a lunchtime discussion of a proposal to ban tobacco advertising throughout the EU, to say that London wants to link its measures with those being considered internationally.
The British change of view has prompted the European Commission to renew attempts to push through the proposal after health ministers effectively shelved it last November.
Germany, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark have been blocking an EU-wide ban while Austria, Italy and Denmark also have reservations about EU anti-tobacco measures.
